💰 What is an Auto-Sweep FD?

An Auto-Sweep FD automatically moves your excess money from your savings account into a Fixed Deposit when your balance crosses a certain limit. This can help you earn higher interest while still keeping your money accessible when you need it.

For example, if your auto-sweep limit is ₹50,000 and your balance reaches ₹70,000, the excess amount may be moved into an FD. When you need money, the FD can be automatically broken/swept back into your savings account.

In this Short, understand auto sweep FD, sweep-in, sweep-out, how it works, benefits, and why you should consider it for idle money.

📌 Always check your bank's specific auto-sweep rules, threshold, sweep amount, FD tenure and applicable interest rates before activating the facility.

snippet.title: WHAT HAPPENED TO FINANCE WITH HARISH - FULL CASE EXPLAINED!
snippet.description:
Finance With Harish Case Explained: What happened to 27-year-old finance influencer V Harish, and why has YouTuber Jason Samuel been arrested?

The death of V Harish, a popular finance content creator from Puducherry with approximately 1.3 million followers, has raised important questions about online harassment, financial influencer regulations and social media accountability.

Here is what we know so far.

**WHO WAS FINANCE WITH HARISH?**

V Harish spent approximately five years creating videos about investments, personal finance and the stock market.

His online brand, Finance With Harish, attracted a large audience across social media platforms.

**WHAT WAS THE SEBI REGISTRATION CONTROVERSY?**

YouTuber and Zemuria CEO Jason Samuel publicly questioned Harish's qualifications and registration to provide investment advice.

Samuel alleged that Harish misrepresented his financial-advice credentials and lacked the required SEBI Registered Investment Adviser (RIA) registration.

However, general financial education and regulated investment advisory services are not necessarily the same thing.

The allegations concerning Harish's specific activities have not been independently established as regulatory violations.

**WHAT DID HARISH'S FAMILY ALLEGE?**

According to a complaint filed by his father, J Vinayagam, Harish experienced sustained online harassment, threats and reputational damage.

The family also alleged that a demand for ₹3 crore was made and that political connections were invoked to threaten Harish.

Harish's original social media accounts were reportedly disabled in September 2026, and a replacement account was subsequently removed.

The circumstances surrounding these account restrictions are under investigation.

**WHAT DID JASON SAMUEL SAY?**

Samuel publicly expressed grief over Harish's death while denying allegations of cyberbullying.

He maintained that he had raised concerns about Harish's financial-advice credentials and consumer protection.

**LATEST POLICE UPDATE — OCTOBER 22, 2026**

Following Harish's death near Chennai on October 20, Kanathur Police registered a case of abetment of suicide.

On October 22, police arrested Jason Samuel in Puducherry.

Investigators are examining digital evidence and the allegations raised by Harish's family.

The case remains under investigation, and no court has established Samuel's guilt.

This case raises an important question: Where should we draw the line between responsible criticism, financial accountability and online harassment?

Share your thoughts respectfully in the comments.

If you or someone you know needs emotional support, contact India's Tele-MANAS mental health helpline at 14416, available 24/7.

snippet.title: पैसे के बारे में ये 20 बातें आपकी सोच बदल देंगी | The Psychology of Money
snippet.description:
पैसे के बारे में ये 20 बातें आपकी सोच बदल देंगी | The Psychology of Money

Why do some people earn a lot of money but still struggle financially, while others slowly build wealth with an average income? The answer is not always about intelligence, salary, or investment knowledge. It is about behavior, psychology, habits, risk, patience, and the way we think about money.

In this video, we break down Morgan Housel’s bestselling book The Psychology of Money and explore 20 powerful lessons that can completely change the way you understand money, wealth, investing, saving, and financial freedom.

You will discover why no one is crazy with money, how luck and risk influence financial success, why knowing when you have enough matters, how compounding creates extraordinary wealth, and why getting wealthy is different from staying wealthy.

This book summary also explains the importance of financial freedom, invisible wealth, saving, reasonable decision-making, preparing for unexpected events, having a margin of safety, accepting change, understanding risk, and avoiding the dangerous traps of comparison, pessimism, greed, and emotional decision-making.

Most importantly, you will learn that wealth is not just about earning more money. Real wealth is about having more control over your time, choices, and future.

What You’ll Learn in This Video

You’ll understand the psychology behind financial decisions, the power of long-term compounding, the difference between being rich and being wealthy, why saving creates freedom, how risk and luck affect your results, why lifestyle inflation can destroy wealth, and how to build a financial mindset that works in the real world.

If you are interested in personal finance, investing, wealth building, financial freedom, money mindset, self-improvement, business, psychology, or book summaries, this video is for you.

snippet.title: The Wealth Strategy Most People Never Learn - Robert Kiyosaki
snippet.description:
Understanding how the rich use debt starts with recognizing that not all debt works the same way.

In this episode of The Rich Dad Radio Show, Robert Kiyosaki challenges one of the most common lessons about money: that becoming debt-free should always be the goal. Instead, Robert explains why financial education—not debt avoidance—determines whether borrowing can help build wealth or destroy it.

Robert breaks down the difference between good debt and bad debt. Bad debt finances liabilities such as cars, credit cards, and consumer purchases that require you to make the payments. Good debt, in Robert's framework, finances assets such as rental real estate, businesses, and productive equipment that can generate enough income to service the debt.

He also explains the Rich Dad concept of OPM—other people's money. With a cash-flowing rental property, for example, an investor may use the bank's money to acquire the asset while tenant income covers the mortgage and operating expenses. The investor uses leverage to control an asset without supplying all of the purchase capital personally.

Robert then takes the strategy further, explaining why borrowed funds generally aren't treated as taxable income and how some investors borrow against appreciated assets rather than selling them. He walks through a cycle of borrowing against an asset, acquiring another cash-flowing asset, refinancing as equity grows, and redeploying that capital.

Finally, Robert explains the concept often called “borrow, buy, die,” including stepped-up basis for inherited assets and why some wealthy investors focus on holding and refinancing assets rather than continually selling them.

But Robert also makes an important distinction: this isn't an argument for reckless borrowing. He stresses reserves, fixed-rate debt, disciplined leverage, sufficient equity, and working with experienced bankers, accountants, and property managers. Debt can create leverage, but without financial education and risk management, that same leverage can become destructive.

The lesson is classic Rich Dad: don't simply ask whether debt is good or bad. Ask what the debt buys, who pays it, and whether it puts money into your pocket or takes money out.

snippet.title: EPF Rule Change: Kya Aapki In-Hand Salary Kam Hogi? #financeindia #personalfinance #business #money
snippet.description:
EPF Rule Change: Kya Aapki In-Hand Salary Kam Hogi?

Salaried employees ke liye EPF contribution ko lekar ek important update hai.

Agar aapka EPF actual basic salary ke 12% ke basis par calculate hota hai, toh is change ka aapke contribution par direct impact nahi ho sakta.

Lekin agar aapka EPF ₹1,800 monthly statutory ceiling ke basis par calculate ho raha tha, toh contribution amount badhne par aapki in-hand salary reduce ho sakti hai, especially agar CTC same rahe.

Is reel mein simple example ke through samjho ki ₹1,800 se ₹3,000 EPF contribution hone par salary par kya effect pad sakta hai.

This content is for educational purposes only. EPF contribution and wage-ceiling rules can depend on applicable EPFO provisions, employment terms and government notifications. The salary impact may vary from employee to employee. Verify the latest official EPFO and government notification before making any decision.

snippet.title: Tax-Free Fixed Income| My Favourite Investment
snippet.description:
Can you really earn 9% fixed income with zero tax?

In this video, I talk about one of my favourite investments — the 8.92% Power Finance Corporation (PFC) tax-free bond that I invested in back in 2013.

These tax-free bonds offered a fixed annual interest income with government backing and tax-free interest under the applicable tax-free bond framework. But there is an important difference between the original coupon rate and the return available to someone buying the bond today.

At the current market price, the effective yield is significantly lower than the original 8.92% coupon. This is why investors should look beyond the headline interest rate and check the current market price, yield to maturity, tax treatment, maturity period and credit quality before investing.

This video also explains how tax-free bonds work, why the 8.92% coupon does not mean a new investor earns 8.92% today, and why long-term investors should not overlook boring but potentially useful fixed-income investments.

This is for educational purposes only and is not investment advice. Always do your own research and consider your financial goals, risk profile and tax situation before investing.

#FixedIncome #TaxFreeBonds #Investing #PersonalFinance

Most people work hard for money, but very few understand how the money game actually works.

In this video, we break down 10 powerful money rules that can help you understand the difference between earning money and building wealth.

You will learn:

Labor vs Capital – Why salary alone may not be enough to build long-term wealth.
Inflation – The Invisible Thief – How rising prices silently reduce the purchasing power of your money.
Defense & Offense – Why controlling expenses is only one side of the wealth-building equation, and why increasing your earning capacity matters.
The Velocity of Money – How reinvesting your money can create a powerful wealth-building flywheel.
The Debt Matrix – The difference between productive debt and debt that can damage your financial future.
Compounding Returns & Skills – Why compounding applies not only to investments but also to your skills and income.
The Protection Shield – Why emergency funds, insurance, nominations and proper financial protection are important.
Your Financial Circle – How the people and environment around you can influence your financial thinking and income potential.
The Rule of 72 – A simple shortcut to understand approximately how long it can take for your money to double.
Time Is the Ultimate Currency – Why the real purpose of money is not simply becoming rich, but gaining greater control over your time.

This video brings all these ideas together into a simple Money Game Masterboard so you can understand wealth creation from a practical perspective.

Whether you are a salaried employee, business owner, young professional, investor or someone just starting your financial journey, these money rules can help you think differently about income, savings, investments, debt, risk, compounding and financial freedom.

Remember: Information without execution is just entertainment.

The real question is not whether you know the rules of the money game.

snippet.title: Why Mumbai Dabbawala Failed After 136 Years? 😭 Business Case Study | Live Hindi
snippet.description:
This video is about "Why Mumbai Dabbawala Failed After 136 Years? | Business Case Study | Live Hindi"

Mumbai Dabbawala is one of the most fascinating business and logistics stories in India. For more than a century, the Mumbai Dabbawalas built an extraordinary lunch box delivery system that became famous around the world for its simplicity, discipline, accuracy, and unique way of working. But what happened to this iconic Mumbai Dabbawala system, and why has a network once celebrated for operational excellence faced such a major decline?

In this video, we explore the complete Mumbai Dabbawala story — from the origins of the Dabbawala of Mumbai to the rise of the famous Mumbai Dabbawala delivery system, how thousands of lunch boxes moved across Mumbai every day, and the challenges that eventually changed this remarkable model.

The Mumbai Dabbawala system became an internationally discussed example of logistics and management. Their simple but highly coordinated Mumbai Dabbawala coding system helped workers identify where each tiffin needed to be collected, transported, sorted, and delivered. Instead of depending on sophisticated technology, the system relied heavily on coordination, local knowledge, discipline, teamwork, and Mumbai's suburban railway network.

This is also what makes the Mumbai Dabbawala case study so interesting from a business perspective. The organization has frequently been discussed in conversations around Mumbai Dabbawala management, Mumbai Dabbawala logistics, Mumbai Dabbawala supply chain, operational efficiency, and last-mile delivery. The famous association between Mumbai Dabbawala and Six Sigma has also helped turn the Dabbawalas into a globally recognized management case study, although some popular claims around their error rates and Six Sigma status deserve careful context.

But a system can be exceptionally efficient and still face structural changes around it.

Changes in office culture, work-from-home and hybrid working patterns, food delivery platforms, changing lifestyles, and the disruption caused by the pandemic altered the environment in which the traditional Mumbai tiffin service operated. A model built around carrying home-cooked lunches between homes and fixed workplaces suddenly had to operate in a very different Mumbai.

So, why Mumbai Dabbawala failed to maintain its earlier scale? What caused the fall of Mumbai Dabbawala? Is the famous Dabbawala system actually disappearing, or is it adapting to a changing city?

This documentary-style Mumbai Dabbawala Business Case Study looks beyond the famous efficiency story and explores both sides — how the system worked so successfully for generations and why the same model is under pressure today.

From the traditional Mumbai lunch box delivery process and railway-based logistics to the coding system, management structure, operational discipline and eventual decline, this video tells the story of one of India's most iconic delivery networks.

If you are interested in Indian business case studies, logistics, supply chain management, business failures, traditional business models, Mumbai history, startup case studies, economics, or stories about how changing technology and consumer behavior can disrupt even highly efficient systems, this video is for you.

snippet.title: Blinkit Expose : How Blinkit Fooling Are Everyone | Business Case Study | 2d Animation
snippet.description:
Blinkit Expose : How Blinkit Fooling Are Everyone | Business Case Study | 2d Animation #Blinkit #BlinkitStory #BusinessCaseStudy


Blinkit is not just a grocery delivery app—it is transforming India’s entire retail industry.

In this video, we explore the complete story of Blinkit: how Albinder Dhindsa and Saurabh Kumar started Grofers in 2013, how it evolved into a 10-minute delivery platform, why Zomato acquired it, and how dark stores became the engine behind its quick-commerce network.

But there is a surprising side to this story. Blinkit continues to invest heavily in dark stores, inventory, staff, delivery fleets, discounts and marketing. So, if grocery delivery has such thin margins, where does the real money come from?

The answer is advertising.

Brands pay Blinkit to secure prominent positions on the homepage, search results and promotional banners. This is turning Blinkit from a simple grocery platform into a powerful retail advertising business.

In this video, you will learn:

• How Grofers started in Gurugram in 2013
• Why Grofers became Blinkit
• How Blinkit’s 10-minute delivery model works
• What dark stores are and why they are expensive
• Why quick-commerce companies face heavy losses
• How Zomato acquired Blinkit
• How Blinkit earns money from advertising
• Why brands pay for visibility inside the app
• How Blinkit is changing Indian shopping habits
• Whether this business model can become profitable

Watch the complete video to understand the hidden business model behind Blinkit’s fast and convenient deliveries.

snippet.title: How India's Day Retail Traders Lost Billions
snippet.description:
Today's financial markets operate at lightning speed, dominated by algorithms and high-frequency trading firms. Nowhere has the impact of this technological advantage been more visible than in India, the world’s largest options trading hub. 

Fueled by mobile apps and so-called finfluencers, millions of everyday investors flooded the market, only to lose billions of dollars while global HFT firms raked in massive profits. Now, as Indian regulators scrutinize the trading of one of those firms, Jane Street, a critical question emerges: should ultra-fast automated trading be seen as an engine for efficient markets, or a game stacked against the average investor?

snippet.title: How Tim Cook Built Apple’s $4.5 Trillion Empire | Untold Story of the Man Who Made Apple Unstoppable
snippet.description:

If you are a copyright owner and believe your work has been used improperly, please contact us at writers@thethinkschool.com for prompt removal or credit. 

VIDEO INTRODUCTION:
In 2011, the world lost the man it considered the greatest entrepreneur alive.
Steve Jobs had taken Apple from the brink of bankruptcy and turned it into the most admired technology company on earth. He built products that changed how people live, and he did it with a charisma that no executive has matched since. He was the closest thing business had to a magician.
And weeks before his death, that magician chose his successor.
The world was not impressed. It was not another visionary. It was a quiet, soft spoken, 50 year old industrial engineer named Tim Cook.
Put the two men side by side and they are opposites in every measurable way. Jobs was the college dropout who became an entrepreneur. Cook was the sincere engineer who spent 16 years inside large corporations before Apple. Jobs was the showman who could hold five thousand people in the palm of his hand. Cook was the man who woke at 3:45 in the morning to read customer emails and study spreadsheets. Jobs was the product genius. Cook was the operations guy who optimised inventory.
So the world reached its verdict. Replace a genius with a supply chain manager and Apple will die. Apple's shares fell on the news, and the mockery echoed across the business press for years.
Now consider the weight on that man's shoulders. You are replacing the most celebrated founder in modern business, and every journalist, every analyst and every fan is waiting for you to fail. Most people in that position would have tried to imitate Steve Jobs.
Tim Cook did the opposite.
Over the next 15 years, the man they called boring took Apple from roughly 350 billion dollars to 4.7 trillion dollars in market value. He grew revenue from 108 billion to 416 billion dollars. He built a services business that now earns 109 billion dollars a year, which is larger than all of Apple was in 2011.
Which raises three questions.
Why did Steve Jobs pick a boring operations guy to replace him?
What made this man so special that Apple grew more than ten times in value?
And what are the business lessons the rest of us need to learn from one of the greatest CEOs in corporate history?

snippet.description:

MySol, whose real name is Solly Soka Madibela, has become one of South Africa’s most talked-about wealthy businessmen. snippet.title: The Battle for Reliance: Mukesh Ambani vs Anil Ambani | Business Case Study
snippet.description:
The Battle for Reliance: Mukesh Ambani vs Anil Ambani | Business Case Study

How did two brothers inherit one of India's biggest business empires and eventually build completely different corporate futures?

This business case study explores the rise, division, rivalry and transformation of the Reliance empire. From Dhirubhai Ambani's vision and the launch of Reliance Infocomm to the 2005 Reliance split, this documentary examines the major business decisions, telecom strategies, corporate disputes, debt expansion and market changes that shaped the futures of Mukesh Ambani and Anil Ambani.

The story covers the rise of Reliance Communications (RCom), Anil Ambani's rapid expansion into telecom, power, entertainment and infrastructure, the MTN merger talks, the KG-D6 gas dispute, and the changing dynamics of India's telecom industry.

We also explore Mukesh Ambani's return to telecom, the acquisition of Infotel Broadband, the creation of Reliance Jio, India's digital transformation and how free voice calls and low-cost mobile data changed the entire telecom market.

This documentary also examines important business lessons about:

• Corporate succession and family business disputes
• Business strategy and competitive advantage
• Debt management and aggressive expansion
• Telecom industry disruption
• Reliance Jio's business strategy
• Corporate restructuring and asset sales
• Risk management and capital allocation
• The rise and fall of Reliance Communications
• Business rivalry and corporate governance
• How technology disruption can transform an entire industry

From becoming one of the world's richest businessmen to facing major debt and insolvency challenges, the journey of Anil Ambani represents one of the most dramatic transformations in Indian corporate history.

Meanwhile, Mukesh Ambani's strategy of using cash flow from Reliance Industries to build a massive digital and telecom ecosystem changed the future of Indian telecommunications.

snippet.title: Patanjali Is in Trouble: What Went Wrong? | The Rise and Fall of Patanjali | Business Case Study
snippet.description:
Patanjali Is in Trouble: What Went Wrong? | The Rise and Fall of Patanjali | Business Case Study #Patanjali #BabaRamdev #BusinessCaseStudy #RiseAndFall 


Patanjali was once one of the fastest-growing names in India’s FMCG industry. Built around Ayurveda, Swadeshi, natural products, and strong consumer trust, Baba Ramdev and Acharya Balkrishna created a business empire that challenged some of the biggest FMCG companies in India.

But what went wrong?

In this business case study, we explore the complete journey of Patanjali — from its early days and rapid rise to the controversies and challenges that put its reputation under pressure.

We cover Patanjali’s growth strategy, Baba Ramdev’s role in building the brand, Acharya Balkrishna’s contribution, the Swadeshi movement, competition from established FMCG companies, the Coronil controversy, misleading advertisement cases and Supreme Court scrutiny, as well as the challenges facing the business today.

Most importantly, this story highlights one of the biggest lessons in business:

Building consumer trust can take years, but protecting that trust is just as important as building it.

Watch the complete video to understand the Rise and Fall of Patanjali and what other businesses can learn from its journey.

snippet.title: Meet the Most Ruthless Billionaire Alive : Larry Ellison
snippet.description:
Download Dhan App Now
https://dhan.go.link/hh98w


Larry Ellison is worth 204 billion dollars and is currently the world’s 7th richest man, yet most people have never heard his name or the name of his company, Oracle. Elon Musk, 27 years younger than Ellison, openly calls him his mentor. 

That alone should tell you something about the kind of person Ellison is. This documentary follows him from a yacht party in Capri in the year 2000, where he deliberately used his boat’s wake to capsize a rival billionaire’s yacht and then laughed about it, to buying a Russian MiG-29 fighter jet he was never legally allowed to fly, to privately owning 98 percent of a Hawaiian island larger than the Maldives. It covers the hostile takeover of PeopleSoft that business schools now teach as a case study in ruthlessness, the Oracle and Bill Gates rivalry that lasted over a decade, and the September 2025 single trading day where Oracle’s market cap jumped by 250 billion dollars and Ellison briefly became the richest man on earth. 

By the end, you will understand why some call him a Corporate Dictator, and why his family may soon control more of the world’s media than anyone else alive.

snippet.title: How a Waiter Built Rameshwaram Cafe | Business Case Study
snippet.description:
How a Waiter Built Rameshwaram Cafe | Business Case Study 

How did a young waiter with very little money go from struggling in Mumbai and working in small food businesses to building The Rameshwaram Cafe, one of the widely discussed South Indian restaurant brands?

This documentary tells the inspiring business journey of Raghavendra Rao and Divya, from their early struggles and the beginning of IDC (Idli Dosa Coffee) to the creation and expansion of The Rameshwaram Cafe.

From a small tricycle food cart to multiple outlets across major Indian cities, this is more than just a restaurant success story. It is a business case study about entrepreneurship, customer experience, food quality, employee training, business expansion and brand building.

The documentary also covers the difficult journey behind the business, the 2024 Brookefield incident, the brand's comeback, its association with major events, expansion into new markets and the launch of Tirtha

📊 Business Numbers
According to reported FY2025 financial data, The Rameshwaram Cafe recorded approximately ₹17.8 crore revenue and around ₹2 crore net profit, compared with approximately ₹11 crore revenue in FY2024.

snippet.title: How Abhishek Bachchan Built a Business Empire After Bollywood Rejected Him?
snippet.description:
In this video, we explore Abhishek Bachchan’s journey from being labelled a “failed actor” to building a successful business and investment portfolio. We look at how his father Amitabh Bachchan’s financial crisis and the collapse of ABCL forced Abhishek to leave his studies at Boston University and return to Mumbai, where he even worked as a Production Boy on film sets.

The video covers Abhishek’s difficult acting journey, his debut with Refugee, multiple box-office failures, and how films like Dhoom and Guru changed his career. We then explore his business journey, including his investment in Jaipur Pink Panthers, Chennaiyin FC, Meridian Tech, Nagin Sauce, Swiggy and Zepto.

We also look at Abhishek Bachchan’s Real Estate investments, including his land near GIFT City, and the growth of the Bachchan family’s property portfolio.

Finally, we explore how Abhishek diversified beyond films and built a strong financial future through Business and Investments.

snippet.title: How Hero Honda Split | Fall of a Legendary Partnership | Business Case Study
snippet.description:
How Hero Honda Split | Fall of a Legendary Partnership | Business Case Study

Why did Hero and Honda split after 26 years of dominating India's motorcycle market? What really happened between Hero MotoCorp and Honda, and how did one of India's most successful business partnerships turn into a fierce rivalry?

This is the complete story of **Hero Honda — from its legendary success to the historic 2010 separation that changed India's two-wheeler industry forever.**

In 1984, India's Hero Group and Japan's Honda Motor Company joined forces to create Hero Honda. With Honda's advanced engine technology and Hero's powerful distribution network, they revolutionized India's motorcycle industry.

From the iconic Hero Honda CD100 and its unforgettable "Fill It, Shut It, Forget It" campaign to the legendary Splendor, Hero Honda became a household name for millions of Indian families.

But behind this extraordinary success, tensions were growing.

Why did Honda launch its own company in India? How did the Honda Activa change the competition? What role did technology dependence, royalty payments, export restrictions, and business disagreements play in the separation?

And most importantly, what happened to Hero after Honda walked away?

In this HINEXP business documentary, we explore:

- The inspiring journey of Brijmohan Lall Munjal and the Hero Group.
- How Hero Cycles became a global bicycle manufacturing giant.
- Why Hero and Honda formed their historic partnership in 1984.
- How the CD100 and Splendor transformed India's motorcycle market.
- The rise of Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India (HMSI).
- How the Honda Activa became a major competitor in India's two-wheeler industry.
- The real business reasons behind the Hero Honda split in 2010.
- How Hero Honda became Hero MotoCorp in 2011.
- Hero's struggle to develop independent technology and expand globally.
- The ongoing competition between Hero MotoCorp and Honda in India.

This is more than just the history of Hero Honda. It's a fascinating business case study about partnerships, competition, technology, brand loyalty, market dominance, and the importance of business independence.

**Hero vs Honda — who really won after the split?**

Watch the complete documentary to discover how two companies built an empire together and why they eventually decided to compete against each other.

**Let us know in the comments:** Which brand do you trust more — Hero or Honda? And what was your family's first motorcycle: CD100, Splendor, or Activa?

snippet.title: They Were the Richest Family in Kanpur
snippet.description:
Pan Parag was the tin you opened at a wedding. The tagline — "Baaratiyon ka swagat, Pan Parag se kijiye" — every Indian over thirty can still finish from memory. The family behind it was the Kotharis of Kanpur, said to be the city's wealthiest. They had two sons. One inherited the pan masala business. The other took a pen company — and a ₹3,695 crore debt across seven government banks.

What you'll find out in this episode:

→ The beginning. Mansukhbhai Kothari was born in Gujarat in 1925 and moved to Kanpur at sixteen. His first business was coconut oil supply. Kanpur in those years was India's textile capital — the "Manchester of the East." Mansukhbhai's luck lay elsewhere. In 1973, he founded Kothari Industries and launched Pan Parag: a ready-to-eat blend of betel nut, cardamom, catechu, and fragrance, sealed in a tin. No paan stall required. Media called him the father of packaged paan masala, though DS Group claims its own product from the 1950s with no specific date. Pan Parag's earliest confirmed date is 1973. Kanpur eventually became known as "Paan Masala City."

→ The advertisement. In the mid-1980s, Mansukhbhai gave Everest Advertising an unusual brief: make Pan Parag something a host offers at a wedding — hospitality, not indulgence — and include an anti-dowry message. Trainee writer Sulekha Bajpai wrote the script. The ad starred Ashok Kumar and Shammi Kapoor — per Storyboard's reporting, the first and last time both appeared in the same frame. The groom's father's "secret demand" turns out to be Pan Parag. Director Prem Krishan said film stars started calling for ad work afterward. Turning a health-suspect product into the symbol of hospitality was, in advertising circles, a deliberate and studied move.

→ The split. Sometime around 1999, the two brothers separated. Deepak kept the pan masala and "Yes" mineral water. Vikram took Rotomac pens — brand ambassadors Salman Khan and Raveena Tandon, tagline "Likhte-likhte love ho jaaye" — plus diversification into greeting cards, real estate, and infrastructure. Hindustan Times quoted friends describing him as flamboyant, dealing in dollars.

→ The fraud allegation. From 2008, Rotomac Global took export-finance loans from a consortium of seven government banks. Total principal: ₹2,919 crore. With interest: ₹3,695 crore. The CBI's case — triggered by a Bank of Baroda complaint — is that the export cycle existed largely on paper. Bills were photocopies; companies in the documents were shells; money traced from one Singapore firm to another and back to Rotomac. A Bank of Baroda representative who checked a Hong Kong address found only a virtual office. Vikram's lawyer called it loan default, not fraud. Vikram himself said he had done nothing wrong and would repay. The account had been NPA since October 2015 — more than two years before the FIR.

→ The arrests. February 2018 — ten days after the Nirav Modi / PNB fraud broke and the country was on alert for fleeing defaulters. Vikram publicly said he had not run away; his Kanpur office was found locked. CBI filed an FIR on February 18. Vikram and his son Rahul were arrested on February 22. Income Tax, ED, and CBI all moved simultaneously. Bail was repeatedly refused. After roughly two years, Vikram received bail on health grounds. On January 4, 2022, household staff found him unconscious at his Kanpur home. He died before any verdict. All charges remained charges.

→ Pan Parag today. Deepak Kothari's name appears nowhere in the CBI case. The two businesses had been legally separate since the split. In 2008, a court-approved demerger transferred the paan masala business to Pan Parag India Limited — private, financials not public. The listed Kothari Products has shifted to real estate and investments. In 2023, the group's fifty-year anniversary was celebrated at Bithoor, with Kapil Dev on stage, a book on Mansukhbhai's life, and Deepak Kothari as host.

snippet.description:
As of 2026, the late South African taxi mogul and co-founder of the South African National Taxi Council (SANTACO), Jothan "Mswazi" Msibi (also known as "King Mswazi"), has become the central figure of explosive revelations at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry. The evidence portrays him as the alleged former mastermind of a powerful, state-entrenched organized crime network known as the "Big Five Cartel" or "The Firm."

snippet.title: 30 Days on a Death Ship (A Mysterious Virus Broke Out, We Got Stranded)
snippet.description:
Come explore Antarctica with me! Message @arctic.antarctic.expeditions on Instagram for trip details and to book your spot. You can also check out Rusarc’s website: https://en.rusarc.com/flysail

This ship is taking us to the world’s most remote island: Tristan da Cunha. But our voyage is about to turn into 75 days of pure torture and put our lives at risk.
Someone among us is carrying a infectious virus called hantavirus. And within just one week, the infection will claim the life of its first victim. Then the virus will begin spreading through the ship. As new cases emerge, more deaths will follow. And the whole world will panic.
This is going to be the kind of journey that turns my hair gray. The most stressful journey of my life is about to begin.

The journey begins with 45 hours of air travel and multiple connections. We’re flying from Istanbul, Türkiye, all the way to Ushuaia, at the southern tip of Argentina. It’s a city known as “the End of the World.” From there, we’ll board our ship for a roughly 30-day voyage to Tristan da Cunha. After that, we’ll spend another 42 days in quarantine.

Come explore Antarctica with me! Message @arctic.antarctic.expeditions on Instagram for trip details and to book your spot. You can also check out Rusarc’s website: https://en.rusarc.com/flysail

This ship is taking us to the world’s most remote island: Tristan da Cunha. But our voyage is about to turn into 75 days of pure torture and put our lives at risk.
Someone among us is carrying a infectious virus called hantavirus. And within just one week, the infection will claim the life of its first victim. Then the virus will begin spreading through the ship. As new cases emerge, more deaths will follow. And the whole world will panic.
This is going to be the kind of journey that turns my hair gray. The most stressful journey of my life is about to begin.

The journey begins with 45 hours of air travel and multiple connections. We’re flying from Istanbul, Türkiye, all the way to Ushuaia, at the southern tip of Argentina. It’s a city known as “the End of the World.” From there, we’ll board our ship for a roughly 30-day voyage to Tristan da Cunha. After that, we’ll spend another 42 days in quarantine.

"Rediscovery" Series ► https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL40Eh9f0PRRXcCkyKxrtRvE3tbmcKYvHr

Visiting the World’s Most Daпgeгous Road: “Karakoram D℮ath Road” (There are casuaIti℮s!) ► https://youtu.be/FryCzL17YRs
Visiting the MOST AIR POLLUTED CITY in the World (Dust Hell) ► https://youtu.be/zC4saZg6sG0
Visiting the COLDEST CITY in the World (-71°C, -96°F) YAKUTSK / YAKUTIA ► https://youtu.be/Fz4ZMLsPzqM
8 Crazy Experiments at -55°C, -67°F (The coldest city in the World: Yakutsk) ► https://youtu.be/ExoOL2lwlWE
World's Poorest Country "Burundi" (I can’t forget the things I saw) ► https://youtu.be/n0gFsHf9cIw

My name is Ruhi Çenet, I'm an independent documentary maker. I go to unique places or meet unique people and investigate or analyze them with a unique approach. My motto is "curiosity is the best guide". Join me, let's learn something different...

snippet.title: I was on the 84th floor of the South Tower - this is how I survived 9/11
snippet.description:
Warning: Contains distressing themes, strong language, and graphic descriptions of injuries.

Janice Brooks had just started her new job in the World Trade Center at Euro Brokers – she had been in New York for just 19 days.

Her office was on the 84th floor of the South Tower.

She had been evacuating when the second plane hit the tower. 

With the help of others, Janice opened the door she had just come through - the stairs were now gone. "All I could see was darkness and flames.”

She remembered the noise of a woman screaming. "A horror film scream that seemed to go on forever and lives in my head for free.”

Janice lost 61 Euro Brokers colleagues on 9/11. They were among the 2,977 people who died that day.

snippet.title: 2006 Surat बाढ़ | जब 1 फैसले ने पूरे शहर को डुबो दिया | Surat Flood 2006 Full Story in Hindi
snippet.description:
2006 Surat बाढ़ | जब 1 फैसले ने पूरे शहर को डुबो दिया | Surat Flood 2006 Full Story in Hindi

अगस्त 2006 में भारत की Diamond City सूरत का करीब 90% हिस्सा पानी में डूब गया था। लेकिन वो पानी सिर्फ आसमान से नहीं आया था।

इस वीडियो में जानिए Surat Flood 2006 की पूरी सच्ची कहानी — कैसे 1 से 6 अगस्त तक Madhya Pradesh और Maharashtra में हुई लगातार बारिश ने Tapi River के catchment area को भर दिया, कैसे 7 अगस्त को Ukai Dam से करीब 9 से 10 लाख cusec पानी छोड़ा गया, और कैसे सिर्फ 4 से 5 लाख cusec क्षमता वाली नदी ने पूरे शहर को अपने अंदर समेट लिया।

अडाजण, रांदेर, वराछा, कतारगाम और अठवा लाइन्स जैसे बड़े इलाके 10 से 20 फीट पानी में डूब गए। लगातार 3 से 4 दिन तक बिजली और पीने के पानी की सप्लाई पूरी तरह ठप रही। लाखों लोग अपनी छतों पर फंसे रहे। अनुमानित आर्थिक नुकसान 20,000 करोड़ रुपये से भी ज्यादा।

इस वीडियो में आप जानेंगे:
◾ Ukai Dam का वो फैसला जिस पर आज तक सवाल उठाए जाते हैं
◾ Rule Curve क्या होता है और उसमें कहाँ चूक हुई
◾ तापी नदी की पानी संभालने की क्षमता आधी कैसे रह गई
◾ 1994 के plague का अनुभव सूरत के कितने काम आया
◾ बाढ़ के बाद Early Warning System और वो बदलाव जो किए गए

सूरत की ये कहानी सिर्फ एक natural disaster की कहानी नहीं है — ये कुदरत और इंसानी फैसलों के मिलने से बनी एक बड़ी आपदा की कहानी है।

💬 कमेंट में जरूर बताइए — अगर 7 अगस्त की उस रात आप Ukai Dam के control room में होते, तो आप कौन सा फैसला लेते?

🔔 ऐसी ही सच्ची घटनाओं के पीछे छिपी असली वजह जानने के लिए चैनल को Subscribe जरूर कीजिए।

📌 यह वीडियो सार्वजनिक रूप से उपलब्ध रिपोर्ट्स, समाचार और तथ्यों पर आधारित है। इसका मकसद किसी व्यक्ति या संस्था को दोष देना नहीं, बल्कि जानकारी देना है।

snippet.title: She Fell 10,000 Feet From a Plane… And SURVIVED! #Shorts
snippet.description:
On Christmas Eve, 1971, a passenger plane broke apart over the Amazon rainforest.

Seventeen-year-old Juliane Koepcke fell thousands of feet, still strapped to a row of airplane seats.

Against extraordinary odds, she survived.

But surviving the crash was only the beginning.

On December 24, 1971, LANSA Flight 508 was flying across Peru when it encountered a violent thunderstorm.

The aircraft broke apart above the rainforest, killing 91 of the 92 people aboard.

Juliane was the sole survivor.

Injured, alone and surrounded by dense Amazonian wilderness, she faced an almost impossible journey back to civilization.

Fortunately, her parents were zoologists, and she had learned valuable lessons about surviving in the rainforest.

One of those lessons would help save her life.

For 11 days, she fought through the jungle before finally reaching rescuers.

This is the extraordinary true story of Juliane Koepcke — the girl who survived a fall from the sky and then survived the Amazon.

**SURVIVAL STORIES — THE AXER STORIES**

Extraordinary people. Impossible odds. Incredible true stories.

AI-generated visuals are illustrative historical reconstructions, not original footage of the incident.

snippet.title: Inside Alaska’s Most Extreme Fishing Ship - Surviving the Bering Sea for Big Cod
snippet.description:
Experience the danger and rewards aboard Alaska’s toughest fishing vessel, the Northern Leader, as it braves hurricane-force storms to haul in record-breaking cod catches.

Join the crew of the Northern Leader, Alaska’s largest longliner, as they face the raw power of the Bering Sea. This state-of-the-art fishing ship is built to withstand 10-meter waves and winds over 100 miles per hour, allowing its crew to fish year-round while other boats run for shelter. Follow Captain Sean Andrew and his team of 26 as they battle brutal weather, tackle mechanical breakdowns, and process up to 750 tons of cod, skate, and pollock on each voyage. Discover how the crew’s grit and stamina translate into some of the highest legal paydays in commercial fishing, with deckhands earning up to $15,000 per trip.

See how the Northern Leader’s advanced technology and relentless work ethic keep the catch flowing, even when disaster strikes in the engine room or factory. Every part of the fish is used, from fillets to livers and stomachs, ensuring nothing goes to waste. With storms raging and massive waves crashing over the deck, the crew’s determination and teamwork are put to the ultimate test. Witness firsthand what it takes to succeed in one of the world’s most dangerous jobs, and how the Northern Leader consistently outperforms the competition, bringing home millions in seafood and setting the standard for Alaskan fishing.

#FishingVessel #BeringSea #AlaskaFishing #NorthernLeader #CommercialFishing #CodFishing #StormAtSea #FishingLife

snippet.title: Nature Khauf
snippet.description:
Welcome to Nature Khauf – जहाँ आप देखेंगे इतिहास की सबसे खतरनाक, डरावनी और दुनिया को हिलाकर रख देने वाली महा-तबाही की कहानियाँ!

इस चैनल पर हम आपको लेकर चलेंगे दुनिया के उन सबसे भयानक पलों में, जब कुदरत के कहर और इंसानी गलतियों ने हंसते-खेलते देशों को मलबे में बदल दिया। सुनामी (Tsunami), विनाशकारी भूकंप (Earthquakes), जानलेवा चक्रवात (Cyclones), बादल का फटना (Cloudburst), खतरनाक गैस लीक और इतिहास के सबसे बड़े अकालों (Famines) की ऐसी इनसाइड स्टोरीज़, जो आपने पहले कभी नहीं सुनी होंगी।

हम सिर्फ तबाही नहीं दिखाते, बल्कि यह भी खंगालते हैं कि कैसे इन त्रासदियों ने दुनिया का भूगोल बदल दिया और देशों की अर्थव्यवस्था (Economy) को अरबों डॉलर का झटका देकर बर्बाद कर दिया।

High-quality visuals, असली होम-वीडियो फुटेज और रीसर्च-बेस्ड थ्रिलर डॉक्यूमेंट्रीज़ के लिए अभी SUBSCRIBE करें और बेल आइकन दबाएं.
